messages:
incident-bot: [P1] service degradation: SableWorks private-vpc (dedicated-pool-7) egress failures to api.sableworks.com — automatic paging triggered -> pagerduty:PD-9876. Symptoms: spike in 502/504 from NLB targets + DNS timeouts from tenant tasks.

maya: oncall-asia here, got the PD. seeing ~30% request error rate to external API from tenant subnets, customer impact: A/B test jobs failing. starting triage.

axel: jumping in, mid-east oncall. can you post the target group health? quick check: 

maya: attaching latest from aws-cli 
```
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:...:targetgroup/tg-12345
{
  "TargetHealthDescriptions": [
    { "Target": {"Id": "10.0.12.45"}, "Health": {"State": "unhealthy", "Reason": "Target.ResponseCodeMismatch"} },
    { "Target": {"Id": "10.0.12.46"}, "Health": {"State": "healthy"} }
  ]
}
```

chen: looks like 10.0.12.45 is flapping. any recent deploys on that pool?

maya: no deploys in the last 6h per deploy-bot. CPU normal, but conntrack table high on that host: `conntrack -S` shows entries ~120k (threshold 128k). may be hitting conntrack exhaustion.

axel: could be source NAT exhaustion on NAT gateway or conntrack on the host. can you check `ss -tanp` and `netstat -s`?

maya: running quick checks now. `ss -tanp | wc -l` -> 54000 connections. `iptables -L -v -n` ok. nat-gw metrics look normal but the tenant route table shows next-hop to a private NAT instance (old config).

sara-m: csm here, I've pinged SableWorks CSM to give ETA; they're seeing background job retries but UI still somewhat usable. asking for holding message.

ops-bot: kube-events: sableworks-pool-7: 15 x HTTP 502 for outbound-proxy job.

axel: aha — private deployment was on NAT instance for egress (we usually use managed NAT). that instance may be overwhelmed. can we confirm instance id?

maya: instance i-0a1b2c3d showing high network tx, conntrack high, syslog shows: `nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet`.

chen: that's our smoking gun. nf_conntrack full -> new connections dropped -> application errors. mitigation options: bump conntrack max on host, temporary route to alternate NAT, or route egress via dedicated proxy in dedicated-pool-7 in another AZ.

eng-sre-lead: priority order: 1) short term reduce failures (route to proxy/failover NAT), 2) add conntrack capacity + restart conntrack (careful), 3) long term replace NAT instance with managed NAT GW. who can make the route change?

axel: i can push a route change to point 0.0.0.0/0 for that private subnet to the standby NAT in az-b. will lower risk if we adjust TTLs and inform DNS? This is just route table change, no DNS impact.

maya: go ahead. posting command I'll run after you give the thumbs up: 
```
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0abc123 --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --instance-id i-0f9e8d7c
```

axel: go for it, i'll monitor.

maya: applied route swap at 3419876610. verifying connectivity...

ops-bot: ALARM cleared: nf_conntrack table pressure reduced on i-0a1b2c3d.

maya: after route swap, error rate dropped from 30% -> 3% over 2 minutes. NLB 502s decreased.

chen: nice. still seeing some slow responses to api.sableworks.com — suspect DNS TTL + client retries. recommend reduce client retry window and keep routing in place for 30m.

csm-jared: drafted customer update for SableWorks: "We've identified transient egress saturation in your private deployment's NAT instance which caused dropped outbound connections. We've routed traffic to a standby gateway and errors have fallen to baseline. We'll follow up with permanent NAT replacement and a post-incident report. Estimated time to full remediation: 6 hours." want to add anything?

maya: add that we're scheduling a config change to use managed NAT (and brief note on increased conntrack limits as stopgap).

csm-jared: sent update to customer at 3419876690. they replied: "Thanks — please keep us updated, jobs are recovering."

eng-sre-lead: OK next steps for ops: (1) schedule migration to managed NAT GW for that VPC (ticket INF-4521), (2) increase nf_conntrack default on AMI to 262144 and roll via bake + ASG, (3) add CloudWatch alert for conntrack > 75% threshold, (4) run postmortem with SableWorks.

axel: i've created the route rollback playbook in case of issues. also registering runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/nat-instance-failover

maya: marking incident as mitigated at 3419876745 — customer impact reduced to low, paging suppressed.

ops-bot: Incident ticket INC-2026 created for follow-ups: assigned eng-sre-lead, due 2026-04-10.

eng-sre-lead: will own postmortem, please capture timestamps and metrics (conntrack, nat instance network I/O, NLB 502s, customer retries).

maya: capturing logs and will upload to incident folder. one quick note — because this is private deployment we need ccs in procurement for cost approval on Managed NAT.

csm-jared: customer asked for planned timeline to avoid recurrence; i'll coordinate with product to prioritize.

chen: final quick commands/observations for the postmortem: 
```
# conntrack dump counts at peak
sudo cat /proc/net/nf_conntrack | wc -l  # ~128000
# syslog snippet
May  4 10:21:12 host kernel: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet
# client error sample
curl -v https://api.sableworks.com/v1/health  
* Connection reset by peer
```

maya: closing thread — follow-ups tracked in INC-2026 and INF-4521. thanks all :thumbsup:
